key_insight: Token consumption in LLM agents is highly variable and cannot be reliably estimated from the start of a task. TokenCast addresses this by forecasting usage as execution unfolds, making predictions that can be updated step by step.
problem_solved: LLM agents often consume very different numbers of tokens across repeated runs of the same task, due to changing tool feedback, branching decisions, and growing context. This makes budgeting, scheduling, and cost control difficult before and during execution.
method: Learns a composable forecasting model for token usage during agent execution.
Updates predictions incrementally as new observations, tool outputs, and intermediate results arrive.
Accounts for context growth and decision-dependent execution paths to estimate total future token consumption.
impact: This helps practitioners better estimate cost, manage latency, and plan infrastructure for agentic LLM systems. It also enables more reliable monitoring and resource allocation for long-running or tool-using AI workflows.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of an LLM agent loop with token usage increasing at each step
Line chart showing predicted vs. actual token consumption over time
Split comparison of low-token and high-token runs for the same task
Icon set for tools, context growth, forecasting, and budgeting
paper_title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
paper_authors: Chaoqian Ouyang, Ling Yue, Libin Zheng, Huanghui Guo, Shengxiang Xu
